title: Muscle Mastery
author: Jussi De Nys
desc:
The purpose of this program is to help lifters build muscle efficiently through a well-structured weekly routine. This split strategically targets each major muscle group with dedicated, intense sessions, tailored to maximize growth while incorporating a balanced frequency across the week, including a mid-week rest day for optimal recovery.

It’s designed for those who want to grow steadily without overloading volume, chasing unsustainable numbers, or risking burnout. You’ll train hard, stimulate every major muscle group effectively, and recover like a pro with a thoughtful mix of workout days and recovery periods.

Each training day focuses on a primary muscle group or a combination (e.g., chest, legs, shoulders, back, arms, and a blood flow/mobility day), allowing for high intensity and concentration. This multi-day structure, with some muscle groups hit directly twice weekly and others supported by indirect work, enhances mind-muscle connection while minimizing overlap fatigue, supported by a rest day on Thursday.

Always aim for the best form and prioritize range of motion over a heavier weight. Lift with the target muscle, not your ego.

You'll be sculpting your physique with a cohesive, adaptable approach.


Feel free to swap out exercises as needed. I personally do most of my workouts in a home basement setup and only visit a public gym on leg days. If you prefer cable machines, smith presses, or gym-based variations—go for it. The real benefits come from the program’s structure and consistency, not from any single movement.

All the best, 
Jussi

ss.note: 30 degree angle on the bench. Lower the barbell towards the clavicle without making contact. Don't lock the elbows out at the top and keep the tempo even and controlled throughout the motion.
Choose between barbell or dumbbell bench press. I have long arms and dumbbells are easier on my shoulders in the flat position. Keep shoulders on the bench, bring the biceps towards eachother.
keep a slight bend in your elbow to prevent injury of the bicep tendon. don't come in all the way as to keep constant tension on the pecs.

ex.note: I do these heel elevated and prioritize range of motion over maximum weight. Go ass to grass and keep the tempo even. Don't drop down into the knees.
curl up and milk the eccentric. This set is to loosen the back and decompress the spine. Do a dead hang for as long it feels comfortable in between or at the end of your reps.
To target the Quads, push with your toes and make sure your heels are at the plane of your sitting surface. If the feet are above your ass you target more of the hips.
Start with active hang and go nose to bar to keep maximum tension on the lats. Bring your elbows down towards your pockets. Add weight if all four sets are smooth with clean form.
Actively retracting and depressing your scapulae (squeezing them down and back) helps to stabilize your shoulder blades, promoting proper shoulder alignment and maximizing lat engagement.

ss.note: Row towards the hips, this naturally brings down the shoulder and targets/squeezes the lats.
Move your elbows up until they are parallel to the floor. Keep hands/dumbells slightly below the elbows.
wider grip for more side delt activation. Narrower grip is more trap activation. Don't raise the bar above the elbows.
This is chest supported on a 45 degree bench. It's a lot like a dumbbell row to target the lats but here you row back on the nipple line and bring the elbows back as far as possible.
30 degree bench. Slow and controlled execution with full range of motion.
Hinge at the hips and lean forward to come close to parallel to the ground. Take a wide grip on the barbell and row the barbell up towards the nipple line.
sit down and rest your forearm on your upper leg for a bigger than 90 degrees angle (arm facing down). Do wrist flexion with the palm facing upwards and use a dumbbell.
Put a towel-wrapped plate on your head and go from neutral neck to raised.

I opted for a lower rep range and heavier weight here. This movement is easier on the elbows and wrist so I like to push the weight on these.
This is a forearm mass builder.
Lay on the bench with your lower arm hanging of the edge acting as extra support and balance. Put a towel wrapped plate on your head and go from neutral neck to raised. perform each side.
take 10% of your current Shoulder day weight for lateral raises and go for higher rep range.
Stay upright with your torso above your hips to target more of the quads.
Create a nice rhythm. This is not a session for PR's or strength.
take 10% of your current Shoulder day weight for rear delt row and go for higher rep range.
Use a narrow grip to bias the upper traps this time instead of the lateral deltoids with the wider grip.

Start with active hang and go nose to bar to keep maximum tension on the lats. Bring your elbows down towards your pockets. Add weight if all four sets are smooth with clean form.
Actively retracting and depressing your scapulae (squeezing them down and back) helps to stabilize your shoulder blades, promoting proper shoulder alignment and maximizing lat engagement.

ss.note: Row towards the hips, this naturally brings down the shoulder and targets/squeezes the lats.
Move your elbows up until they are parallel to the floor. Keep hands/dumbells slightly below the elbows.
wider grip for more side delt activation. Narrower grip is more trap activation. Don't raise the bar above the elbows.
This is chest supported on a 45 degree bench. It's a lot like a dumbbell row to target the lats but here you row back on the nipple line and bring the elbows back as far as possible.
30 degree bench. Slow and controlled execution with full range of motion.
Hinge at the hips and lean forward to come close to parallel to the ground. Take a wide grip on the barbell and row the barbell up towards the nipple line.
sit down and rest your forearm on your upper leg for a bigger than 90 degrees angle (arm facing down). Do wrist flexion with the palm facing upwards and use a dumbbell.
Put a towel-wrapped plate on your head and go from neutral neck to raised.

I opted for a lower rep range and heavier weight here. This movement is easier on the elbows and wrist so I like to push the weight on these.
This is a forearm mass builder.
Lay on the bench with your lower arm hanging of the edge acting as extra support and balance. Put a towel wrapped plate on your head and go from neutral neck to raised. perform each side.
take 10% of your current Shoulder day weight for lateral raises and go for higher rep range.
Stay upright with your torso above your hips to target more of the quads.
Create a nice rhythm. This is not a session for PR's or strength.
take 10% of your current Shoulder day weight for rear delt row and go for higher rep range.
Use a narrow grip to bias the upper traps this time instead of the lateral deltoids with the wider grip.
30 degree angle on the bench. Lower the barbell towards the clavicle without making contact. Don't lock the elbows out at the top and keep the tempo even and controlled throughout the motion.
Choose between barbell or dumbbell bench press. I have long arms and dumbbells are easier on my shoulders in the flat position. Keep shoulders on the bench, bring the biceps towards eachother.
keep a slight bend in your elbow to prevent injury of the bicep tendon. don't come in all the way as to keep constant tension on the pecs.

ex.note: I do these heel elevated and prioritize range of motion over maximum weight. Go ass to grass and keep the tempo even. Don't drop down into the knees.
